pages.text: $(bold)Blood Manipulation$(): blood as a blade, piercing ten thousand foes.$(br2)Folds $(bold)Piercing Blood / Convergence / Supernova$() into a single technique (only taking up 1 technique slot).$(br2)$(bold)Controls$(): press $(bold)C$() to unleash the current move; press $(bold)F$() (the reversal key) to cycle the current move through Piercing Blood → Convergence → Supernova.

$(bold)Piercing Blood$(): spend 5% of your max health and fire a beam of blood along your facing direction that pierces the 20 blocks ahead of you (blocks do not stop it): every target pierced takes (1 + Affinity/100) × (Cursed Energy Output + spent health × 5) damage once.$(br2)$(bold)Convergence$(): spend 7% of your max health; lock on to a target by line of sight and five pillars of blood surge around your body, dealing 5 hits in total, each equal to Piercing Blood's single-target damage ÷ 2.$(br2)$(bold)Supernova$(): spend 10% of your max health; lock on by line of sight and spawn a tiny blood orb at the target that explodes after 0.8 seconds (no block damage): center damage = (1 + Affinity/100) × Cursed Energy Output × spent health × 10, falling off linearly with distance.

All three moves $(bold)ignore invulnerability frames$() (armor can still reduce them) and trigger material combat traits as usual; in Creative mode no health is spent (the damage is still calculated from the theoretical cost), and a move cannot be used when your current health cannot cover its cost.$(br2)$(bold)Cursed energy cost$(): Piercing Blood = base / 2; Convergence = base × 5/3; Supernova = base × 5/2.$(br2)Convergence and Supernova only spend health when your line of sight actually hits a target (the cursed energy is deducted regardless); Piercing Blood fires in a straight line and needs no lock-on.
